newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Tuesday due to improved market sentiment with investors optimistic about the near-term trend, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 20,560 yuan ($2,477) per tonne, rising 510 yuan. It opened at 20,500 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,080 and a high of 20,600.
December rose 310 to 20,120, January 380 to 20,440, March 610 to 20,670, April 660 to 20,700, May 600 to 20,630.
Combined volume rose to 176,860 tonnes from 136,660.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange encouraged long position holders in Shanghai and strong sentiment made copper stick to high levels.
"Few investors dared to hold short positions," one trader said. "This resulted in large amonuts of stop loss buying orders on the market today."
"Confidence of long position holders improved very much with expected further rises in the next few days," he added.
Traders said copper was likely to keep an upward trend in the short term though a brief techncial correction was possible due to sharp rises in the past few days.
"Despite sharp rises in the past few days, open interest has decreased day by day, indicating many investors were afraid of an imminent technical correction," a second trader said.
"But the whole market is unlikely to fall due to improved market sentiment unless there is major negative news," he said.
Aluminium January rose 20 yuan to 13,500 and February gained 130 to 13,410. Combined volume rose to 160 tonnes from 20.
